title: Improving the Self-Efficacy of African American Parents in Infant Supine Sleep
brief_summary: This is a research study of African American parents/caregivers of newborns. The purpose of this research study is to learn what type of educational materials about infant safety and safe infant sleep are most effective and acceptable to parents and caregivers. The investigators will compare the responses of parents who receive enhanced materials to the responses of parents who receive the ordinary materials that are currently in use.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:-

\- Self-identified AA adult parents and primary caregivers (≥ 18 years of age) of newborns ≤ four weeks old at the time of the infant's first office visit to the pediatrician.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Foster parents and temporary guardians:
* Prior study participants:
* Parents without a reliable phone number:
* Parents without ready access to a DVD player: an ownership of a DVD player,
condition: African American Infant Sleep Beliefs and Practices
